subject: Re: Allocation approach for IP indemnity — proposal on scope & notice owners
messages:
From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@nimblehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Cho <d.cho@cholegal.com>
Date: 2025-03-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: NimbleHealth redline + question on indemnity split

Rishi — attaching our redline for the MSA and order form (see attached). Two quick asks from our side so procurement/legal can assess: 

1) We want the contract to clearly split responsibility for third-party IP claims arising from (a) Customer content (datasets, prompts) vs (b) Model-generated output. Specifically, NimbleHealth will defend claims that result from our customers' uploaded training or proprietary content; Redwood to defend claims that arise from model output or your provided models. Can you confirm Redwood is comfortable with a clean bifurcation?

2) Evidence custody and notice routing: we need an operational owner for notices and a clear chain-of-custody for evidence (logs, model snapshots, prompt history). Please propose (a) who at Redwood will accept notices, (b) expected SLA to acknowledge, and (c) where evidence will be staged.

Daniel and I put a quick matrix in the attached spreadsheet that maps claim types to evidence types. Happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Klein
Head of Legal Ops, NimbleHealth
Attachments: NimbleHealth_MSA_redline_20250319.pdf (pdf), evidence-ownership-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

---

Note: Original redline includes a proposed carveout for open-source model components and for claims tied solely to customer-supplied training data.
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Daniel Cho <d.cho@cholegal.com>
Date: 2025-03-19T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NimbleHealth redline + question on indemnity split

Sara — thanks for the redline and the matrix. Appreciate the clarity. High level response below; want to make sure we put actionable items into the order form so procurement can route quickly.

Summary proposal (Redwood position):
- Scope split: Redwood will accept responsibility for third-party claims that allege infringement arising from our provided models or our model weights/architecture and from model-generated outputs where Redwood-controlled model inference produced the output. NimbleHealth will accept responsibility for claims arising from customer-supplied training data, customer-provided models, and any modification of outputs by your downstream tooling that is outside Redwood runtime.
- OSS carveout: we agree to an explicit OSS/third-party license carveout (we won't defend claims solely about upstream OSS license compliance).
- Defense vs. coordination: Redwood prefers to provide defense under scenarios we control (model-origin claims); for mixed claims we propose a joint coordination clause with a technical evidence custodian appointed per claim.

Operational asks from Redwood: 
1) Notice owner: Redwood proposes a single mailbox for legal notices: notices@redwood.ai. We'll commit to 48 business-hour acknowledgement for notice receipts and provide a triage contact within that window.
2) Evidence staging: Redwood will provide a secure evidence staging bucket (s3://redwood-evidence/nh-{deal}) and a read-only snapshot of inference logs & truncated prompt history for the relevant timeframe. We expect NimbleHealth to produce any customer-supplied training data and chain-of-custody records.
3) Forensics SLA: initial evidence handoff within 10 business days of agreed scope; longer timelines for archived datasets.

Action items: 
- Kimberly, can you confirm that the evidence staging approach above matches our data retention policies and whether 10 business days is feasible operationally?
- Ben, can you flag any commercial implications (insurance/escrow) so I can loop Nemra in procurement if needed.

Sara/Daniel — if you can confirm the split above (or highlight redlines you cannot accept), we'll prepare a short redline that implements these operational commitments in the order form.

Thanks,
Rishi
VP, Legal & Business Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: NimbleHealth redline + question on indemnity split

Rishi — quick operational confirmation and a tweak on defense control mechanics.

Operational confirmation: the s3 staging bucket approach is OK but we need the following in the order form or a referenced runbook: 
- Minimum evidence package: inference logs (time-bounded), model config & version, hash of model weights (if applicable), and a redacted prompt history that preserves sequence but removes PII.
- Access: NimbleHealth's counsel will get time-limited read-only access; Redwood forensic engineers will have upload privileges for derived artifacts (token traces, model snapshots).
- Retention: we can snapshot and retain evidence for 90 days by default (longer if the customer has a paid forensic retention add-on).

Defense-control tweak: for claims that clearly arise from Redwood model output, Redwood will propose to lead defense but will provide regular status updates and technical callbacks to NimbleHealth counsel. For mixed claims, we recommend a short escalation clause: the parties may agree within 5 business days whether Redwood will lead defense; if no agreement, the parties will appoint independent technical neutral to allocate responsibility for technical evidence collection.

Timing: our infra and security teams confirm the 10-business-day evidence handoff is achievable for active logs; archived datasets may require 20+ business days depending on retrieval processes. Please set expectations with NimbleHealth accordingly.

I've updated the evidence-ownership-matrix spreadsheet (see attachment) with the minimum package and retention defaults.

Kimberly
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Rishi/Kimberly/Sara — quick note from counsel: NimbleHealth is comfortable with the bifurcation as framed below, subject to two narrow edits: (1) a mutual cooperation clause that requires NimbleHealth to provide custody materials within 10 business days (we can accept 10 for logs, 20 for archived datasets) and (2) a tweak to the OSS carveout so it is limited to upstream license claims (not claims that arise from your proprietary model adaptations).

If Redwood can accept the cooperation timing and the upstream-limited OSS carveout, NimbleHealth will sign off on putting this language into the order form and we can proceed with an execution redline. We'll also need a DocuSign link once the final redline is ready.

Next steps: Rishi — would you like Redwood legal to prepare the execution redline that incorporates:
- notice mailbox (notices@redwood.ai) and 48hr acknowledgement
- evidence staging & retention defaults (90 days snapshot)
- 10/20 business-day handoff timing and the neutral appointment process for mixed claims
- OSS carveout language limited to upstream license claims

If yes, we'll aim to circulate a redline by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Daniel Cho
Counsel to NimbleHealth
